utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and in the booths assisting us. Before we give the opportunity to the Prosecution to call the next witness, I think we still have to deal with the documents. Madam Registrar, could you please, after having called the case, assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could you guide us through the...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2309A, a report on criminal technical examination of the site at the Markale market. P2309A.1, the English translation. P2172 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp. Let me just ask you, there are a few documents which you did not tender under seal, and it really takes quite an effort to find in that document what you shouldn't find perhaps, but do you think that it should be admitted under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would only ask that the name on the bottom of the front in the middle be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm afraid that's not possible. When you show it on the ELMO, you can easily do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just consult one moment, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you then also pay attention to 2172 and express the Prosecution's view also on D67.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please the Court, in respect to the Exhibit 2172, we would have no objection if it's received by the Court under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: D67, if my records are correct, is a drawing which the Defence counsel asked the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not as far as I can see. As far as I can see, it's an on-site criminal forensic investigation related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Subject to the Defence it being something proffered by them, I would ask that be received on the seal as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2172.1, the English translation. P3665, a sketch drawn by the witness. P2171, a report submitted by Borislav Stankov. And P2171.1, the English translation. P22 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to P2171, there had been a paragraph with some illegible passages. And I had asked -- I realise that I'm not in a position to instruct the language section because they are not under our control. I asked them to revise the translation excluding the areas as ordered by the Court. I received this morning the revised translation and a letter attached to it in which it is expressed that they cannot, as a matter of the governing rules, omit to translate anything which is legible on a document. And they are asking or suggesting that the Court, if it sees it fit, could ignore that part of the document which they think is illegible and which would affect the context of the rest of the paragraph. I'm afraid I could not demand of them that they do as was indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, it would be acceptable for this Chamber, since it is a specific part where only the first sentence remains for this Chamber to consider, that if you take the original translation as it existed and you blacken the remaining part of that paragraph so that we cannot read apart from the first sentence of that paragraph what the translation would be, that would be acceptable to be admitted. Since we cannot read the original language, so we have a -- we would then have a translation that is partly blackened, especially that part we would not accept. I think that can be easily done. It doesn't have to be done on this very moment. If you do it, let's say, somewhere over the next hour. Then we would first have the original entered into evidence, and then you offer the translation but part of it unreadable for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could please prepare that. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2247A, report on forensic investigation of site where mortar shells landed. P2247A.1, the English translation. P3644.MS, map marked by witness. D67 under seal, a report on-site criminal forensic investigation bearing ERN number 0070 -- I apologise. Bearing ERN number 0036-2616. The English translation, D671 under seal. D68, a diagram. D69, a diagram drawn by the witness. D70, three pages of diagrams. D71, annex 6 of the UNPROFOR report, page 768 and 769. D72, a videotape. D73, a videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Am I right that in the diagram made by the witness has not been copied yet, so who is going to take care of that? Perhaps you, if it's still in your hands, you will provide both the Chamber and the parties with copies of that diagram. Thank you, Madam Registrar. They are then all admitted into evidence. And I note that 2171 and translation, 2172 and translation, D67, are under seal. Then, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases you, Mr. President, Your Honours, there is another matter in respect to the exhibits, that is going back to the testimony of Sead Besic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Court had indicated that perhaps if the Exhibit D64, which was a tape which the Defence had produced in Court but which we had just received, was identical or contained everything which was in the tapes previously played in Court, then perhaps that comprehensive tape could be put in evidence. I have to advise the Court that it is not. The tape D64 has on it the entirety of the videorecording of the investigations of the 4th of February, 1994, which was played before the Court. Thereafter, it has only a part of the investigations of the 5th of February, 1994, which was played before the Court. Before that was presented, there were two other videos played in respect to the investigations of the 5th and 6th January [sic]. That was P2279, which was a cut version of an original document, original video, which is P2279A. The Court had asked that a video be prepared of only those parts which were played in the Court. That has been done, and we have designated that P2279B. And that would have been comprehensive for those parts of the Markale investigation which was videotaped and which had been played before the Court up to the testimony of Sead Besic. Other parts have now been played subsequently of the same tape, and therefore, subject to the Court, of course, I would recommend that the Court receives in evidence the full uncut version which has everything that was played in Court. And that would be P2279A, as well as the one tendered by the Defence, D64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that on the record. So it's your request that apart from D64 tendered by the Defence, that 2279A, that's the uncut -- the complete version, is also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll give a decision on that after the break. It's not an urgent matter at this very moment as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp, for your additional information. 2279A has been available to the Defence in a prior stage. So if there would be any objection, Ms. Pilipovic, but I'm not aware at this very moment, then please let us know just at the end of the -- just before the break, or if you say I can only do it during the break, please let us know so we can give a decision on the admission in evidence of a videotape 2279A. Yes, if there's nothing else, Mr. Stamp, who would be the next witness you would call?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Next witness is Witness AF.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right if I expect it to be Witness AK?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: AK, I beg your pardon. Thanks, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness AK is protected by a pseudonym and by face distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would mean that when she enters the courtroom, we have to take special caution that she'll not be...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that the booth is aware of the measures to be taken when she enters the courtroom. Mr. Usher, would you then, please, bring in Witness AK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you may know, this Court has granted protective measures in your respect, and that means that we are not addressing you by your name but by a pseudonym. We will call you Mrs. AK. That's the special name you got in this courtroom. Before testifying in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make the declaration, and the text of the declaration will be handed out to you by the usher now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mrs. AK, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. I checked that the protective measures are effective. That means that your face cannot be seen on the video images, and that we'll not mention your name. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours. If I may proceed by handing to the witness a document which I ask be handed to her in such a way that the camera may not pick up what is on it. It's Document P3671.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Witness AK, I'm going to ask you to answer me "yes" or "no," and do not tell me what is written there. Just simply, do you see your name written on that document; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see your date of birth written on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P3671, Madam Registrar, is admitted into evidence. It's the name sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal, yes. I apologise. Ms. Pilipovic, it had not been shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And my apology as well. Oversight on my part as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Madam, do you live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For about how long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: 35 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm afraid I see the answer on the transcript, but I didn't hear it. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: 35 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It might have been a technical fault. I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you live in Sarajevo during the conflict between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, without telling us your exact address in terms of the street, could you tell us which quarter or district of Sarajevo did you live at during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And were you married with children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. I'm married, and I have two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you -- I withdraw that. Do you recall speaking with an investigator of the OTP on the 18th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you put on a map that he presented you an approximate location of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you saw that map, you'd be able to identify it, would you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, I ask that the witness be shown P3666, with the -- with a part of it obliterated. Could you show that to the Defence as well before you show it to her. Could you put the map on the screen there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, is that the map that you were shown by the investigator in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. We believe the answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. AK, if you turn to the right, the interpreters have difficulties in hearing you so. The usher will assist you to speak into the microphone even if you're looking on the map. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe you said that this was a map you were shown in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The map that the Defence has been given is marked. It has a mark at the bottom where it says Stari Grad, so I just want to know if that is the case with all the maps, to avoid any confusion later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's a marked map, Mr. Stamp. I see some orange and red markings on it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. On this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On this one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There's an orange mark on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe you said this was a map you were shown by an OTP investigator in 1995. Was it the map you were shown by an OTP investigator in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you mark on it the approximate location of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the map which you have to your side, could you just point to where you marked as the approximate location of your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are pointing to the red X on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I do understand that you're fully aware that you're just asking the witness the approximate, not the -- especially in view of the protective measures. The booth was asking whether everything is okay. But as far as I understand your questioning, it's just the approximate area, yes. Please proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, from where you lived approximately how far was the confrontation line between the two parties of the conflict, that is the confrontation line between the Bosnian Serb army and the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: About 500 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And was that to the north, south, east, or west? In other words, may I rephrase it, was that confrontation line to the north of your house, to the south of your house, to the east of your house, or to the west of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I think north.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in the course of the conflict, what was the condition of life in Sedrenik in respect to shelling and sniping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The conditions were very hard. We dare not come out by day so that we went at night to fetch water. We would go out at 11.00 and wait until 5.00 in the morning. And after 5.00, even if we didn't get any water, we had to go back without it and then come back the next night because that was when the snipers would set off in action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, do you know any particular community which lay to the north of where you lived beyond the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us of sniping. What was the condition of life in Sedrenik during the conflict in respect to shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Very difficult. There was frequent shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you or was your home ever affected by the shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Once in the evening, at 7.00, we were having our supper, and the shell hit 5 metres in front of our house. Now, there is a big boulder there, and it hit the boulder. All the windows burst. All our things were thrown out of the house. We were seven in that room. Myself, my husband, my youngest son, my daughter-in-law, my two sisters. Fortunately, there was shrapnel all around, but no one was hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall when this occurred? Do you recall the year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Just a moment. I think it was 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember what part of that year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: September, I think. Maybe October.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you hear shells being fired during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was this a frequent or infrequent observation that you made of hearing shells fired? Did you hear it frequently or infrequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say if you heard the sound of the firing coming from any particular community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. From when -- they were fired from Mrkovici, then one could hear them better when they were fired from Mrkovici than from some other parts of the city. When they came from this part, I could hear them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was Mrkovici with respect to where you lived and with respect to where the confrontation line was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The confrontation line was above my house, not in front of the house but behind the house. And Mrkovici was in this direction, that is, to one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you could hear them better from Mrkovici than when they were fired from other parts of the city. Could you say what other parts of the city they were fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From Trebevic, too, often.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Trebevic I take it is on the other side of the city, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. It would be in front of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could just get the geography clear. You live in an area of Sedrenik, which is a hill overlooking urban Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And from where you lived, you could look above the city towards Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in respect to the shelling which came from Trebevic, and I'm asking you about the period from August 1992 -- from September 1992 to August 1994, in particular, or I'm asking you to confine everything you say to that period, September 1992 to August 1994, did you see or observe anything in respect of the shelling as far as Trebevic is concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I did. In daytime, I could see with the naked eye the barrels on Trebevic, and I could see fire coming from Trebevic, fire that was aimed in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you hear anything when the fire came from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. I could hear it when shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you hear when shots were fired from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question is: What did you hear when you say you could hear it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It was the gunfire. I could see barrels, and I would hear these shots. And then I could see the first shell hit somewhere in or around Stari Grad, then we would get down to the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you also heard shell fire coming from Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there any military installations or soldiers in the vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, none. It was just neighbourhood, an area with civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to cast your mind to the 5th of February, 1994. Can you recall that day? Was there anything that was to happen that day which was of any personal interest to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was of personal interest to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That day, my father was to be buried. He had died on the 3rd of February and on the 5th was the funeral. He lived in Zenica. It was very difficult for us because we could not leave Sarajevo at the time. We were under complete siege. So I came out to the terrace the balcony, because I was having it very hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That day, were you home alone or were you there with other persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I was alone. My husband worked for the [redacted] and he was on duty all the time. He was on reserve all the time. My younger son was at school, so that I was all alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, at about what time did you go out on the balcony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It was around 12.00, around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, while you were out on the balcony, did you hear anything in particular after 12.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. I heard a shot being fired, but I didn't move. I just stayed on the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say "a shot," could you tell us what you heard? A shot sounding like what? What did the shot that you speak of sound like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, that sound, that sound was the regular sound that I heard always both from Mrkovici and from Trebevic. It's like when a plastic bottle bursts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let me clarify one thing: It was 12.00 mid-day or 12.00 midnight? I want to get the time straight when you went on your balcony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Noon. Perhaps it wasn't noon exactly, it could have been plus minus. But sometime between 12.00 and half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, that sound which you heard, which you said you had heard before coming from Mrkovici, could you describe the sound as best as you can, or could you tell us what it sounded like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's a sound as like when a plastic bottle explodes. There is a burst, there is a bang, and then you hear a buzz.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let us -- you said it sounded -- you said "I heard a shot being fired." It sounded like a shot from what? That is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Like a plastic bottle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did it -- from what type of weapon did it -- did this shot sound like it was fired from? Heavy or light weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That sound was always made by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you heard this sound which you describe as always being made by a shell, did you observe anything in the vicinity of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did anything happen in the city after you heard the sound of the shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us what happened in the city, what you noticed in the city.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That day was exceptionally quiet. There was no shelling the whole morning so that everybody went about their chores, going to the market to buy something. So did my son, because we had -- my youngest son -- and we needed a pot of milk or something on the market. So my son went to the market. And then I heard the sound of that shell, and I immediately thought -- rather, I saw -- I could see part of the cathedral, so I assumed it was the market. I knew my son was at the market at the time, my older son.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you notice from the cathedral? What could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I'm rather high up. My house is on a slope, and it was a clear day where I lived, because we're on a hill. But in the city, it was rather cloudy. It was rather overcast. And nevertheless, I could see smoke coming out from that part of the market, lots of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which market is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how long after you heard the shot of the shell from Mrkovici did you see the smoke coming from Markale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, it didn't take long. Could have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you estimate the time? Just an estimate, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, a couple of seconds. Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What do you mean by "a couple"? Could you just give us an estimate in numbers? We know it's an estimate. We know you can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I don't know. Could have been five seconds, say. Really, I can't judge. I can't assess that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said that that day was a clear day, and at least in Sedrenik, and there had been no shelling otherwise that morning. But on other days, was this the first time you had heard shells being shot from the area of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And was this the first time you had observed smoke or anything happen in the city after shells were shot from Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That day?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, I'm speaking generally. Generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Oh, no. All shells throughout the aggression, I could see every single shell where it fell in the city from Trebevic, from Mrkovici, and from other parts of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said you were concerned for one of your sons who had gone to the market. Did you do anything after you saw the smoke coming from the area of the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: My sister lives next to the cathedral, so I called my sister that very moment and asked my brother-in-law to go out and try to find out what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How did you call your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: By telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And was your son hurt in the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No. At that moment, when the shell fell, there is a supermarket across Markale, and he was trying to buy something there so that he was in the supermarket at the moment when the shell fell so that he wasn't hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The area of Mrkovici, can you say which of the parties in the conflict? Was it the Bosnian Serb army or the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina which controlled Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Our army had no access to Mrkovici at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it by that answer you're saying the area of Mrkovici was under the Bosnian Serb army control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the areas of Trebevic from which you saw shelling into the city, can you say which party of the conflict controlled that area of Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Serb troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I have a moment to confer with my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was any of your family or relatives injured in the explosion in the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: None of my proper family.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Anybody -- I don't want to use the expression "improper" family. Was anybody close to you, do you know, injured at the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, we had a number of friends, acquaintances, but none of my family strictly speaking. Oh, excuse me, sorry. My brother-in-law was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Madam AK. My friend may have questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. AK, you'll now be questioned by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. AK, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, and I believe that you've already confirmed the fact, that on the 18th of November, 1995, you've given to members of the OTP a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: By signing the statement, did you confirm that the declaration, that statement, contains what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if after the month of November 1995, you talked once again with members of the OTP and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I believe that it was in 1998. I have had a conversation with them again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you interviewed on the 24th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And on the 3rd of August, 2000, were you interviewed by them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Believe me that I do not remember of the dates. I know that I was interviewed. We had exchanges, but I cannot remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the map that my learned colleagues showed you, you have indicated the approximate place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You lived there with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had a younger son. That also means that you must have had an older son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, where did your eldest work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: He was working in the water company, and it was a duty -- working duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was your son a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, later he became a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that he became a soldier, when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Not right away. When the aggression began, there was a mobilisation, and then he was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did the mobilisation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Five months later, after the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what do you mean by "aggression"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: As of the 1st of March, 1992, I believe that he was already in the army in June.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you mean when you said "as of the 1st of March, 1992"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, during that period of time, he was still working at the water company, was working duty. He was working actually at that water company. He was an employee of the company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did the mobilisation take place? When was he drafted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Five months later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So as of the month of June 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what military unit did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The 105th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "105th," can you explain a bit closer what it is, it is the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your son live with you in the same house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the positions were? Where did your son go to the front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: My son was in the demarcation line of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to what brigade did your son belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The 105th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the front line was in Sedrenik. What was the distance of the 105th Brigade, the brigade in which your son was, from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: About 600 metres. In fact, they were right under the Spicasta, so I presume that must have been the right distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your son also bore weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Later. Not right away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What were the weapons that he was issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: A rifle. It was an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did he also wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No. They only received uniforms in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When he would go to the front line, how long would he stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: He would go in the evening, and then he would come back in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would he come back home for lunch, or did he eat with the rest of the army somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, he was only going in the evening. He would leave at 7.00 p.m. and he would come back at 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And where was your husband? Was he on the front line as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: He was a reserve employee. He worked at the company, Poditrastovi. He was working for the water company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far was the water company, the reservoir, from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: About 500 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That water reservoir that your husband took care of, was that the reservoir that supplied the inhabitants of Sedrenik with water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: When there was water. It was actually not for the civilians. It was for the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you told us that that reservoir that your husband had to take Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. care of, and I presume other people as well, was supplying the citizens of Sedrenik as well as the hospital. Which hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The Kosevo Hospital under the Podhrastovi, in Podhrastovi.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993, how often was your son absent? How often would he go to the front line? Was it every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, it was every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When your son would come back from the front line, would he tell you that at that place where he was, that there were some fightings going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: He would never tell us these things, but we were able to hear nevertheless and we were also able to see what was going on. We knew when we heard shots. They couldn't fire back. They didn't have any weapons really, because one automatic rifle served for three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This is what your son had told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: We knew this. Everybody knew this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your son tell you, would he tell you, how many weapons did they have within their brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, he wouldn't tell us anything, but we would know because the other members of the group from the neighbourhood were going there. And we knew that they didn't have any weapons. We also knew that they had to share a rifle. They had to share -- three people had to share the same rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your son ever tell you that he was holding the positions of Grdonj and Sedam Suma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, he wasn't there. He was not at those positions. He was right under the Spica. That was his position.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the distance between the VRS positions and the lines where your son went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: About a hundred to 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the following: If we talk of Sedrenik, in relation to Sedrenik, where is Mrkovici with regards to the cardinal points? Would you be able to show us on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes, but I do not have a map before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to submit to the witness the map P3666.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to Sedrenik, would you be able to show us where -- or in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, not the house. Sedrenik is here, and Mrkovici is situated over here in this direction. Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far is Mrkovici from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I don't know precisely, but I presume that it must be about 1 kilometre to 2 kilometres at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just for the sake of the record, the witness was pointing in the direction of the right top corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Later on, with your leave, I will show the witness a map that shows Mrkovici so we can all clearly see where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But since this map is more clear, I would like to ask a few questions in relation to this map. I would like to ask the witness to show us on this map the area of the Markale market and to show us -- in respect to the house of the witness, I would like to ask the witness to mark with a black marker the Markale market to show us where it is in respect to her house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you be kind enough to take a black marker and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. AK, may I just draw your attention. If you are leaning over to the map as you do it now, so then the technicians have difficulties with the face distortion because they have to show the map, but at the same time not show your face. So if it would be possible for you just even if you point at something, to sit a bit back so that your facial distortion still functions and that your face is not to be seen when you're leaning over to the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm terribly sorry, but my glasses are not the right ones. When I left, my glasses were broken. So I had to take these, but they don't really correspond to my -- they are not really clear for me. They are not the right glasses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us where the Markale market is situated on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What street is it on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Titova Street. May I place this map in front of me?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can. And please draw a little circle around the place where the Markale market is. You may take a black marker, circle it, and write number 1 in the middle of it or next to it. Witness, were you able to find it? Did you circle the spot? Please draw a small circle and indicate it with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now where your house is with respect to the market? You can do this by drawing a straight line with the marker, if you can show us the general direction of your house by doing this, please. You may draw a line from the market towards your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From your house, would you be able to show us where Mrkovici is. So in relation to your house, draw a line with the same marker, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please put an arrow to indicate -- on that line, you can put an arrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness indicated the location of the Markale market. She indicated it with the number "1." And from the red cross that indicates the approximate position of her house, she drew a line in the direction of northeast, and with this line, she indicated the direction of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know what is the distance between your house and the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I believe approximately 700 kilometres [as interpreted] as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you said that Mrkovici in relation to your house is 2 kilometres away --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, no, no. About a kilometre and a half. I don't really know with precision.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But what is Mrkovici? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Mrkovici is a neighbourhood. It's actually a village in itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, but I went to Crepoljsko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between your house yourself and Crepoljsko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's very close to Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is an upper Mrkovici and lower Mrkovici, so Gornji Mrkovici and Donja Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you told us that Mrkovici is a distance of about a kilometre and a half from your house, then in metres or kilometres, what is the distance from your house to the Markale market? Is it 1 kilometres or a thousand metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I said about 700 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, in the transcript, it says it's 700 kilometres, which might be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what is the distance between the Markale market and your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's not that far. Approximately -- well, from my house, the street goes right down to Bascarsija, and from Bascarsija to the market, it's not very far. It's -- the distance is shorter than from my house to that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in the part of the city called Sedrenik where you live, you were able to hear and see a very -- shelling at -- very frequently. Can you tell us how frequently were you able to hear shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It would occur every day, sometimes two shells would land, sometimes three. In that more closer area, more narrow area, but very often there were lots of shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you saw each shell that landed on the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From what vantage point were you able to observe these shells fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From my house, from the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you were in your house and not in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, if the city was shelled, I would then stay in the house. But whenever I would hear a shell falling close by, I would then go down to the cellar. But even from the cellar, I was able to see where the shells were landing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you would see shells land, could you tell us in what part of the city were the shells directed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: For the most part, in the Stari Grad area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the damage caused in those parts of the city by the shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The damage was quite important. The old city, Stari Grad, was quite damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to show us on the map from which part of the city of Sarajevo were you able to see the direction of which the shells would land on the Stari Grad area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From Mrkovici, let me find Trebevic. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With a black marker, could you please show us the direction from which the shells that you were able to see were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Here. Here, here. Trebevic it's over here. No, we don't see Trebevic on this map. This is Vrace, this is that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With a black marker, would you please indicate those areas for which you say that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's this part here going all the way up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are drawing what exactly right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From Vraca, the shells were directed. And here Trebevic is not shown on the map. This is the Trebevic area. It was coming from the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness showed Vrace --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please tell us where Vrace is by indicating a V. Witness, mark with a V the area for which you said it was Vrace.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for the transcript, the witness drew a line from Vrace indicated with a V, a straight line going all the way to her house to show us where the shells were coming from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Those shells would come from here, from Vrace, and they would land in Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please then indicate Bascarsija with a letter B. You can mark a big letter B -- capital B so we can see it well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Trebevic they would also come from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please indicate the line with a T. In the lower part, mark a T so we know we are talking about Trebevic, and please show us the parts of the city on which the shells landed, those shells that were coming from Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please draw a very large circle around that part of the town to show us where the shells that came from Trebevic landed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what is the name of that part of the city? Is it Hrasnovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, it's Brdo here. It's this area here. For the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's not an objection. But I think the pace is such that we perhaps will not get enough for the record to record what these markings are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, I think it's a good suggestion to take it part by part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to explain everything for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, right, so you drew a line in the middle of the map, but the lower part you indicated with a T the location of Trebevic. So from that direction, the witness drew a line and also drew a large circle around the general area for which she said to us that Sedrenik was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a minor point, but just for the record, the T represents, according to the witness, the direction of Trebevic, not the location of Trebevic. She said Trebevic is not on the map. But I think she was showing the direction from which it came and not that the T shows where Trebevic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, could you please clarify that with the witness, Ms. Pilipovic. Apart from that, Ms. Pilipovic, how much time would you still need? I'm asking this specifically because for the next witness, we might need some time to prepare the courtroom. So I wonder if it would just be a matter of a couple of minutes, then we could ask the booth whether we could continue or not. So that we can use the break for preparing the courtroom for the next witness. If not, please indicate. So how much time you still need. And I bring to your attention that the examination-in-chief took approximately 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my cross-examination will be no longer than 35 minutes, but I believe that I still have 15 more minutes, and I will attempt to finish the cross-examination within that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you want to stay within 35 minutes, you have no 15 minutes left any more. Let me just guide you. On my laptop, the cross-examination started at 1 minute after 10.00, and on my laptop time, because the time is not always the same, you are now at 10.31, so you used 30 minutes. If you think you could finish in five minutes, I would see whether we could continue. If not, please indicate so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to finish in ten minutes, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then ask the booth, since for the protective measures, the technicians will need some time. I assume it will take approximately 20 minutes. If we now would have a break, then continue for another 5 or 7 or 10 minutes, and then we would need another 20 minutes' break immediately afterwards. So if it would be acceptable to you, I'd rather now see whether we can finish. Of course, if not, then... May I have an answer from the booth? I know that I'm now and then asking a lot of you. Yes, I don't hear anything as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No problem, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is also valid for the French booth? Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. For the transcript, T indicates the direction that the witness indicated to us as being the direction of Trebevic. She also drew a very large circle around an area from which from Trebevic the shells landed. The circle indicates or shows us Sedrenik, that general area, in which the witness also lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on that map, did you also draw another line to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what direction that indicates? What is the direction from which you tell us that the shelling came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It's Colina, Colina Kapa it's called.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to write the letter C around it, so letter C.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness just indicated the letter C. It's the direction of Colina Kapa, and it's from that direction that the city was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what part of the city was shelled by drawing a circle around that part in question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of that part of the city? And indicate the letter of that part of the city, write a letter down. What is the name of that part of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Mihrivode.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Then please write an M next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness drew a line on the map and indicated the direction of Colina Kapa, and from that direction, the part of the city was shelled, and it's the part of the city for which the witness drew a circle, and that's the part of the city called Mihrivode indicated with an M.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You told us that on the 5th of February, you heard something being fired, a projectile being fired.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us from what direction and how far was the distance from the place where you were standing that you heard that firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: About a kilometre to a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you hear after that when you told us that you heard firing of a projectile? What did you hear afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I heard something being fired. I heard a sound, and then I heard also shooting above my house. I also heard that same sound, and then I saw where the shell landed. And I also saw this huge smoke coming from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that this lasted 5 seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: A couple of seconds. You may determine it yourself. But it really happened quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is the sound that you heard over your house or above your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: It was a sound that was quite familiar to me. I often heard that sound at the same height going in the same direction, and it was always the same sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you compare that sound to a sound that's familiar to all of us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Well, first, like a burst of a plastic bottle, and then a buzzing sound. It was very fast. And then shots being shot above the house, or some kind of an explosion happening above the house, as if something was exploding, parts were being taken apart. And then I would see the shell land.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you told us that when you were on the balcony you saw what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I heard the sound, and I saw where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the shell flying over your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, I wasn't able to see it but only heard the sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So witness you're telling us that you first heard something being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And then you heard over your house a sound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. I heard first a firing sound, and then above my house sort of an explosion, and then buzzing again up until the time the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you're talking about the explosion or the firing that would take place while it was still over your house, was it the same sound as when you heard the shot being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, the sound was louder.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a sound that resembled something being fired, I mean the sound that you heard when the projectile was fired, was that the same sound that you heard while it was over your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, it was a much louder sounds. It was a more strident sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You mean over your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you heard this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I am aware that you're trying to finish within the time indicated, but I think it goes a bit too quick at this very moment. Mrs. AK, the interpreters cannot follow you if you -- since you are speaking the same language if you are just answering the question immediately. So would you please take a tiny little pause before answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us, Witness, that you heard a sound above your house, and it was louder than the sound that you heard when this projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell us what was the weapon from which you heard this projectile being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I am not a military expert. I do not know from which weapon the projectile was fired. But I know that during the aggression there were those sounds. I am not an expert in weapons. I cannot give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You talked to us about the aggression. Can you explain to us, what do you mean by this word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I shall try to do so. According to me, an aggression is what happens when innocent civilians can feel and hear shots being fired. We didn't know the reason for this. We didn't know why.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I believed that it was the JNA at the beginning of the war. Then the VRS, and then the followers of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us if on the area of the city of Sarajevo the BiH army was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: I never met with the army. I was just a simple civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what about your son? Was he a member of the army of the BiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes. But later he was drafted. The whole city was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. President. That would be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Stamp, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You indicated that the market was on Titova Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that the same as Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say where the market is in respect to -- may I phrase the question this way: Do you know of Vuka Karadzica Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say where the market is in respect to Vuka Karadzica Street and Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Right next to the market --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter begins over.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From the market to the Karadzica Street, it's not very far.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far from the market to Vuka Karadzica Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: Approximately 400 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, where is the market in respect to both Vuka Karadzica Street and Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: The market is on Marsal Tito Street and Karadzica -- Vuka Karadzica Street is to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To the left facing where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: From the market left -- away from the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you find Vuka Karadzica Street on that map and point to it. I know you have problems with your glasses, but do your best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Stamp, that the glasses might cause some problems or whatever other circumstance. The Chamber would find it acceptable if you ask for confirmation whether the street you just mentioned is where it is indicated as such on the map. I don't know how to do it. But I think we could...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I could try it this way:

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Have you found it, firstly? Have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: No, I didn't find the street. But it is this area here, somewhere here between Mejtas and -- it's somewhere here, but I just can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you put the map on the ELMO, please. Could you find Marsal Tito Street on that map and point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AK
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point -- have you found Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I have to establish that the witness has great difficulties in looking at this map. I do not exactly know for what evidentiary purposes both parties have asked about the location of Markale market. If it is to establish objectively where the Markale market was, then perhaps we could find another solution. If it was in order to find out whether the witness knew where the Markale market is, we have to face the problem that she seems to have difficulties in finding her way on this map. She might know, but quite apart from this map, where Markale market is. So may I invite the parties to let me know what they actually wanted to establish by putting these questions to the witness. Was it where the Markale market is, or was it anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That precisely is what I wanted to clarify, where the Markale market is on the map. However, having regard to the observations made by the Court, I think I could leave it at that. Because the witness is really having difficulties, I perceive, reading that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it might even be possible that the parties compromise on where the Markale market is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. I hope that by some time next week we will have agreed upon a map where certain landmarks or certain positions are noted, for example, the tunnel which you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For example, yes. Ms. Pilipovic, any observation in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my questions to the witness regarding the marking of the location of the Markale market were asked merely to check the credibility of the witness, to clarify the facts related to the incident she claims she had seen, and seeing the smoke burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Mr. Stamp, may I understand that this concluded your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. AK, since the Judges have no additional questions to you, and since you've answered the questions both by the Prosecution and the Defence, this concludes your testimony in this courtroom. You'll understand that it's very important for this Court -- I apologise. It's very important for this Court to hear the testimony of those who were present at the relevant times and places to hear their answers to the questions of the Prosecution and of the Defence. So we thank you very much for coming here and making it possible for us to take those decisions that we'll finally have to take. I know it's quite something to come the whole way from Sarajevo to The Hague to testify in this Court. We therefore thank you very much for having come to us. And I wish you a safe journey home again. Thank you very much. Yes. We'll then have a break until 25 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first give a decision in respect of tape 2279A. Is there any observation to be made, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence does not object to the tendering of this tape, but we wish to point out that this is not an authentic tape either. It is also just a working document. That is one thing that we wish to point out, that this is not the authentic tape. But we do not object to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All right, then tape 2279A will be admitted into evidence, but the Chamber notes that it has been played to the Chamber only up to the scene of the morgue. So with this annotation, the tape is then admitted into evidence. Mr. Stamp, are you ready to call your next witness? That would be -- yes, we still have to deal with the documents of the Witness AK. Madam Registrar, could you please guide us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3671 under seal, pseudonym sheet. Exhibit P3666 under seal, map marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. These two documents have now become exhibits and are admitted into evidence. Then Mr. Stamp, are you ready to call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will be Witness AF, protective measures, pseudonym, face, and voice distortion, if I'm well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please lead the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand? Yes, can you hear me -- Mr. Usher, would you please put on the microphone. Yes, seek the right channel. Yes. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. AF, I will call you AF since this Chamber has granted you protective measures in your respect. Mr. AF, before giving testimony in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that declaration of which the text has been handed out to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Usher, could you please point the microphones in such a way that -- no, no, no. I'm mistaken. It's because of the voice alteration. I apologise. Mr. AF, you'll first be examined by the Prosecution, then by counsel for the Defence; and if there are any additional questions by the Judges, they will be put to you as well. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. May I proceed with your leave, Mr. President and Your Honours, by asking the witness to be shown Document P3667, and shown in such a manner that it is not depicted or picked up on the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my apologies. Perhaps I wasn't following closely enough. Did the witness take the -- make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Witness, without telling me what is actually written on the document, could you just answer two questions for me, and just answer "yes" or "no." On the document do you see your name written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see your date of birth written there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind both counsel to put the microphone off when the witness answers the question. Yes, to put it on when you put the question; put it off when the witness answers it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Witness AF, do you live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And for how long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I was born there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you have lived there since you were born there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, there was a conflict which took place in Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the earlier part of the conflict, in 1992, did you join any particular group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And for how long did you serve in the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, some seven or eight months. As a matter of fact, until my wife got killed. And then, because I was a single father of a child underage, I was relieved of all duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you remember when your wife was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: On the 14th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you remember where you lived with your wife? The district, not the precise address, just the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the Stari Grad municipality, and that particular neighbourhood was and is called Vratnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the vicinity of where you lived with your wife, and I take it your child -- maybe I should ask the question, did your child also live with you and your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In this community of Vratnik where you lived with your wife and child, were there any military positions in the immediate vicinity of where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like you to tell the Court the circumstances in which your wife got killed. Firstly by telling us about what time of the day did the events occur.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It happened in daytime. I don't remember the exact hour. I don't remember the hour, but it could have been between 12.00 and 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where were you at that time? Were you at the family home or were you elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: At that time, I was at my wife's uncle, which are two houses below the house in which my wife was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, your wife's uncle's house, which you said is two houses below, how far in terms of distance is your wife's uncle's house from the house in which your wife was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: About 15, 20 metres on the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened at the house in which your wife was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: The shell hit a house below the house in which my wife was at the time. It hit the roof of that house, and shrapnel got in through the window.
