And one of the pieces hit her here, as they said, in the main artery. And as soon as that happened, I dashed out of that house, that is, I had to run some 15, 20 metres. I was barefoot, and I had to run over broken glass and shards. And as I entered Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that house, she was already losing consciousness. So I picked her up and carried her out of the house, and a car happened to be around. So we tried to take her to the hospital, to the main hospital at Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop there. The house in which she was at at the time, whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was my father-in-law's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if she was there alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, she wasn't alone. Her mother was there. And my daughter was there, too. Her mother was also hit, hit up here, but she did not suffer any ill effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was her mother hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: The forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you tried to take her to the main hospital at Kosevo. Did you manage to take her to the main hospital at Kosevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I managed to put her in that car, and we started down the street. I reached a flat part, which is called Kovaci, but nobody could get through there, because it was either a sniper or a pot, that is, an anti-aircraft gun which was firing at it from Trebevic. So this crossroad was closed. Nobody could pass through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The sniper or anti-aircraft gun was firing at that street called Kovaci, or firing into that street called Kovaci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You couldn't pass. So as a result, did you go anywhere instead with your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I couldn't get through, so I turned back to Vratnik where we had a local infirmary. I mean it had been there for 15 or 20 years already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you reached to that local infirmary, in what condition was your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Unfortunately, she had expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the time when you arrived there, had she yet expired immediately at the time when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: She died in my arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us that shortly after that incident, you left the army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you take up any particular occupation after you left the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Before the war, I worked as a taxi driver so that after that, I resumed that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, where did your parents live during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: They also lived in Stari Grad, in Sedrenik neighbourhood community. Beneath -- at the foot of Spicasta Stijena. The locality is known for that Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, your wider family, I mean outside of your immediate parents, brothers, and sisters, were they in any way affected by the war in the Sedrenik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Why, yes. Many of them. I cannot give you the number. But quite a number of them were wounded and killed. It is an area where many families have the same last name, over 20 households all sharing the same surname. So they are all part of one extended family.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, during the conflict in the period I would like to ask you to direct your comments to, that is from September 1992 to August 1994, were any civilian members of your wider family killed or injured in the Sedrenik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes. My father was one of them. He was killed. My mother was wounded. And she is an invalid for life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, may I remind you that it's really necessary to put your microphone off whenever the witness answers the questions. It's of major importance for the effectiveness of the measures you've sought.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Apart from your mother and father, were there other civilian members of your family that were killed or injured in the region in the area of Sedrenik during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes. For instance, my uncle's child, 9 and a half, 10 years old, I'm not quite sure, was killed. And several elderly relatives of my father's were also killed. And I don't think I should list all the wounded because there's quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What caused them to be killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: My father was killed by a sniper. My mother was wounded by a sniper. This little boy was killed by a shell. He was killed by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did the sniping into Sedrenik come from? Can you say from which area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the shelling, can you say approximately where the shelling came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From behind Spicasta Stijena. It's called Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The area of Spicasta Stijena where the sniping came from was under the control of which party to the conflict? Do you know? Was it the Bosnian Serb army or the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: The army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the area of Mrkovici, do you know which army controlled that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Serb troops were in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The area in Vratnik where you lived with your wife and child, do you know where the shelling frequently or normally came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From the direction of Borije. It is a clearing, a clearing called Borije.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you told us that your father was killed by a sniper and your mother was shot so that she is now an invalid for life. Were you there when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, I arrived later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was that later the same day or another day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour after it happened, an hour and a half. Perhaps as soon as I heard that it had happened, I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you have a sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the area where your father was killed, were you told about what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: My sister told me the whole story.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us what she told you happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: Since there was no water in the house, because a shell had hit the manhole with the water meter and everything and destroyed it all, my father had to go every morning from our house to our neighbour's house to bring water.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, how old was your father at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was he a member of any army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, he wasn't a member of any army. He was a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you were interviewed by investigators of the office of the Prosecutor in February 1996. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you recall drawing for them a small diagram indicating the circumstances in which your father was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, I'd like to hand to the witness Document P2424. And I respectfully ask that a certain part of that document be covered. Just the part with the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Yes, that should be covered. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that document a copy of the map which you drew for the OTP investigator in 1996 -- of the diagram, I beg your pardon, of which you drew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the diagram be placed on the ELMO, with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, there's a pointer there in front of you. I'd like you to point to the structure on the drawing which is marked by number 1 on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What does that indicate? Could you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That is the house where my parents lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, on the map, on the diagram, there is a structure marked by a number 2. Could you point to that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what does the number 2 structure indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That is my neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the top of the map -- of the diagram, you have a number 3 marked there. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: These are the positions of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which area is that indicating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It's part of Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately how far was that area from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, about a hundred, 150, maybe as much as 200 metres more or less. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the diagram you have, you had drawn a number 4. What does that number 4 indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It indicates where the water fountain was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And between that water fountain marked 4 and the house of your neighbour marked 2, you wrote 3M. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That is the distance from the house to the water fountain, and the distance is in metres. So it's about 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that your father would go to fetch water. Would he go to fetch water at the water fountain that you have depicted marked number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: He would go there every morning. He will go to get water every morning, and he would take this same route that's indicated on the sketch. There's a road actually from -- a little path from my house to the water fountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, on the day that your father was killed, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: He had left the house to go towards the water fountain, the path that is drawn on the sketch. When he arrived to the water fountain, the sniper from Spicasta Stijena hit him. He was able to call my mother. My mother and my sister ran along that same pathway to help him. Unfortunately, -- or rather, however, my sister ran first. She was able to get to this house that's indicated with the number 2. But unfortunately my mother was hit by the sniper bullet at the spot that's indicated with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was your mother hit? What part of her body was she hit at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: She was hit in the leg above the knee, the upper portion of the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And where was your father hit? In what part of his body, that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: He was hit in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After your mother was shot, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: She was able to make it to the house that's indicated with the number 2. Then the sister started to call the neighbour, and those cousins that were there, the relatives that were there that were able to hear, they really came right away. One of them managed to run across, because there was firing in a nonstop fashion from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This firing in a nonstop fashion was fired towards where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Towards the spot where my father was and towards, let's say, the structure indicated with a number 2. It was really directed towards that structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened after your neighbours came out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: One of my relatives was able to run across that area that's indicated from house number 1 going to house number 2. So it's about 15 metres. The distance is about 15 metres from one house to the other. He saw that my father didn't give any signs of life, didn't show any signs of life. And he probably just assumed that he had died on the spot. He started, therefore, to help my mother. I don't know how, but they were able to stop the haemorrhage. They were able to press on her leg. And then two more relatives came over. They ran over. They put my mother on a blanket, and at the very moment when they were crossing, or while they were carrying my wounded mother on that blanket, while they were trying to bring her to a car that was ready to bring her to the hospital, I draw on this sketch the area. So it's right here. There's sort of a small hill. I don't know how to explain it to you really. There's a sort of a boundary. And right there, the sniper fire was being heard again. The sniper started shooting again at that very moment while they were carrying my mother on that blanket. Everybody fell down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for the record, he pointed to a spot on the map -- on the diagram, which is a line ending with two arrows, one of them pointing to the number 5. After the shooting continued to this area where they were trying to carry your mother to, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: When the fire was opened, they all fell down to the ground. Fortunately, they were able to carry away my mother and nobody was wounded. They actually brought her to the hospital. And once again, somebody had to run towards my father to pull him out of there. One of my relatives ran away -- ran across, and he found in that house a sort of a plastic cover. From the house number 1, somebody threw to him a very long rope. He placed my father on that plastic, and he tied him. He tied the rope to the plastic, and he was able to pull my father to the other side. My father had already died.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During this time, did the fire from Spicasta Stijena stop, or did it continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: During all that time, they were firing from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, hand to the witness Exhibit P3131.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please assist Mr. Stamp, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, before it is handed to him, there is a photograph marked 2 at the bottom right of that photograph. I'd ask if the side view of a face be covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall being in the area of your parents' house with investigators from the OTP in March of 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did these investigators take photographs of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like you briefly to tell us what each of these photographs depict. First, have a look at the photograph numbered 1. If you could put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where on this photograph is Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is what we call Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, Your Honours, the witness pointed to a line of trees going across the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Towards the bottom of the photograph, there is a wooden structure. And that is in the foreground towards the bottom of the photograph. What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It's the fence of the house in which my neighbour lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is this a house marked 2 on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Have a look at photograph number 2. Again, what does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is also the house of my neighbour, and we also see Spicasta Stijena again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you point to where Spicasta Stijena is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again, for the record, the witness points to a line of trees going across the middle of the map [sic] from the right to approximately the centre of the map [sic]. And if I should correct myself, it's a photograph clearly, not a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at photograph number 3. What does that depict, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is where my neighbour's houses are, and we can see a path going -- road actually going to Mrkovici. It's the road that, before the war, one would take to go to Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point to that road, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you do so again, a little bit more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness indicates to be the road what appears on photograph number 3 to be a white line goes across the middle of the map [sic] from about the centre of the map [sic] to the right. I keep saying "map;" photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, could you perhaps please clarify. I saw the witness making movement from right to approximately the centre of the photograph, and then back to the right again uphill. It's not clear from your description whether you mentioned just one part or the two parts. Could you please clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point again to the road and slowly move the pointer along that road as it is on photograph number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the witness has indicated a line running from a wooded area to the middle of the extreme right of the map [sic], across the right of the map [sic] to the bottom of a slope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have some doubt on whether this is a clear description for the transcript. Would it assist you if I would try to describe what was indicated by the witness, as starting at the very right-hand side of the picture, approximately one-third from below a thin white line, going from there to the left, ending approximately in the middle of the picture. Then turning sharply to the right going uphill, up to where a few trees can be seen approximately in the middle of the photograph at the very right-hand side of that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am very grateful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you have a look now at photograph number 4. What does this photograph show on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Those are the houses of my neighbours, and over the treetops, we can see Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. President, if I need to make any description for the record. I think that should be pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please look at photograph number 5. Is this a -- could you just tell us what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This photograph depicts houses, and we can also see once again the road going on to Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To the left of that photograph is a wooded area. Where is that area? What is that area called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It depicts the area of Sedam Suma, seven forests, seven woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for the right of the photograph, from top to bottom of the photograph, there is another wooded area. What does that depict, can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It also depicts this larger area that we used to the seven woods or the seven forests; in the original language, Sedam Suma.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And photograph number 6, have a quick look at that one. The structure in the foreground to the right, that is what, can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is a fence surrounding my neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the middle of the photograph, there is a wooded area. Where is that, can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is that wooded area called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Sedam Suma, seven woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at photograph number 7. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: This is the shed right next to my parents' house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And beyond that, there's a line of trees in the background going across the middle of the photograph. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It's behind my house, and we see once again Spicasta Stijena at the very top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point on the map [sic] to where you see Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to an area in the background running in the middle of the map [sic] to the right, a wooded area in the background of the map [sic] running from about the middle of the map [sic] to the right middle of the map [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And photograph number 8, could you have a look at that, please. What does this photograph indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Once again, this is the house of my parents, my neighbours, and relatives, and we also see Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On this photograph could you point if you can the house of your parents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, before asking the witness to do so, wouldn't you think that this could or might affect the protective measures? If you want his identity to be kept secret, I can imagine that pointing to it on a picture instead of describing it might make the protective measures less effective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could do it not on the ELMO, and ask the witness perhaps to describe the house in such a way that we can follow it, if you see the picture. But that it could not be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well I think the text will be broadcasted, but if you say three houses with a red roof and one with a black roof, which not true, it might be understandable for anyone with a pictures in his hands and not understandable by anyone without a picture. Could you please try guide to the witness in whatever way, let's say by counting houses or whatever manner you used. Mr. AF, I suggested to Mr. Stamp that you not point at the house of your parents on a screen on a picture because this might make your protection less effective. And perhaps guide you in another way how to indicate the house of your parents. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You heard His Honour, Mr. President. Could you describe as best you can the position where your parents' house is on this map -- on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: We cannot see it on this picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That solved the problem, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you describe the position of -- well, may I ask this first: Is your neighbour's house, the house which you marked on the diagram number 2, on this map -- on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the area on these maps -- on these photographs which you describe as Spicasta Stijena, was this the area from which the firing came when your father was killed and your mother was incapacitated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, may I just ask you, because we changed the sequence of breaks a bit, how much time would you still need approximately so that I would know whether to have a break now or perhaps after you concluded your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 10 to 15 minutes would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 10 to 15 minutes. I then suggest that we continue for another 10 minutes, have then a break of 20 minutes, and then continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. As it pleases you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. If this is, of course, acceptable for all three booths, the second part which usually takes one hour and a half would then take approximately five quarters of an hour. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the date that your father was shot and killed, can you remember that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: 31st of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in the immediate vicinity of your parents' home, are there any military positions there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I wish to take you now to the 5th of February, 1994. At around mid-day on that day, did you go anywhere in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: What am I to say now? Coming from Vratnik. Well, I came from Vratnik every day, because there I used to live with my wife, and I would go to my parents' house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you go to your parents' house on the 5th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, that day, I was in the garden washing the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At about what time were you in the garden washing the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was around noon, that is, around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were in the garden washing the car, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Could you clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were in the garden washing the car, did anything happen that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Why, yes. One could hear -- one could hear a shot being fired from -- I suppose from some heavy weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did the sound of a shot of a heavy weapon come from in respect -- well, just tell us where did that sound come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From behind Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know which community is behind Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say at approximately what time you heard this shot from a heavy weapon coming from behind Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, it was around there. Could have been between 12.00 and half past approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said you had been in the army. Had you heard heavy weapons being fired before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you hear while you were in the army these heavy weapons being fired frequently or infrequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, excuse me, which army? Which troops do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Any troop. Any army, any troop, did you hear heavy weapons being fired while you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: While I was a member of the Yugoslav People's Army in 1984, then I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your experience in the Yugoslav army and early in the army of the conflict of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, can you say what was the sound that you heard coming from behind Spicasta Stijena sound like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, it sounded like some -- like some blow from a barrel. I don't really know how to explain it. One could hear it being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did the sound sound like any particular weapon to you, from your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, I would say a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, there are heavy mortars, medium-sized mortars, and light mortars. Did it sound like any one of these types of mortars? Could you answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, I don't think I can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, shortly after you heard the sound being fired from behind Spicasta Stijena, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, from the moment when it was fired, and within some 10 to 15 seconds -- I'm not sure -- one could hear a detonation in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you hear any other shells fired in that area at around that time that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you eventually go into the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, after -- after perhaps half an hour, an hour, after I put my car in order, I went to my taxi stop, to my taxi stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is your taxi stand in the urban part of Sarajevo, the built-up part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And when you went to the taxi stand, did you hear what had happened at the Markale market that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, because this taxi stand is right next to Markale, then of course I heard from fellow taxi drivers what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you went to your parents' house, your mother's house in Sedrenik that day, for what purpose did you go there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Why, to see my parents, of course. Simply I don't know of any more important reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was your father alive at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I take it you went to see your mother. About how often would you visit your mother during that period of early 1994, late 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Since she had been severely wounded, I went to see her every day. She was bedridden for a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, Mr. President, Your Honours, is the examination-in-chief of this witness. May it please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. AF, we'll first have a break of 20 minutes, and then you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you -- I know that you're always trying hard to be as efficient and effective as possible. We all know it's Friday. We also know that next week, it will be the time for the videolink. May I just ask you to see whether it would be possible to conclude the examination of this witness today. I'm just asking, you understand. But you're fully entitled to perform your task as good as you can. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I expect, though, that I shall be met with understanding if it takes 5 or 10 minutes longer than our working hours, that is, quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance. We'll then have a break until five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you would like to address the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Just briefly, may I beg your permission and your special indulgence, notwithstanding I said the examination-in-chief had ended, just to ask a couple of questions and put a document to the witness. It would just take two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you know that I urged Ms. Pilipovic to... Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, at the same time the photographs you were shown were taken, that is, on the 27th of February, 1996, did you also mark a map for the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you mark on that map the approximate location of your mother's home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you also mark on that map the approximate location of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you saw that map again, would you be able to identify it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, could the witness be shown P3668 with a part of the name covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the map be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point out for us the approximate location -- or may I put it this way: Could you point out for us a place on the map which you marked as the approximate location of your mother's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to a small X in the upper right corner of the map just above where it says "Sedrenik" on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you also point out where you marked for the OTP investigators the positions of the VRS, the Bosnian Serbian army at Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that the area where there's a line drawn laterally across the map with four circles above it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Then now, Mr. AF, you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which part of Sarajevo did you live in prior to the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: In Stari Grad, municipality of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was Vratnik part of the municipality of Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So did you live in Vratnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: After the war broke out, I moved over to my father-in-law's because at Sedrenik, I lived in a small house where I was not safe. And I didn't think that my child and my wife would be safe there. And that is why I moved over to Vratnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, after the conflict broke out in 1992, when did you join the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a month before the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when was the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you join the BH army, which month of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I think it was May.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that May 1992 when you joined the BH army, which military formation did you join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I think it was 15th Mountain or something. I can't exactly remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "15th Mountain," do you mean a brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: More or less I'm saying -- I'm telling you I'm not sure. I know it was something mountain. Whether it was 15 or something, I've no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you report, to which part of the city and where was the command post of this 15 mountain brigade when you reported there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the command post of the 15th of Mountain Brigade where you reported and asked to join? When you joined the BH army, where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, there was headquarters in some garage or something at Vratnik, something sort of headquarters. It was just a plain garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether this garage was in the building where people lived, that is, was it a residential building or an office building? In what building was the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was in a yard next to a house, next to a building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And who was the commander of that 15th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you say that was at Vratnik, where were the positions at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Vratnik of that brigade which you belonged to? If it is easier for you, I'll give you a map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Just a moment. As a soldier, I never went to any of the positions, to any of the front lines, as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was your role as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Why, we guarded -- we stood night watch around some streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which are the streets where you stood watch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: You mean the names?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In which part of the locality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, in Vratnik, on all streets. There would be two men responsible for doing rounds of these streets to see that nobody gets in there after the curfew.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did you have when you used to guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: At that time, I had a make-shift pistol made of a water pipe in to which only one hunting bullet could fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And other members who -- other soldiers who stood watch, what kind of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: In the early days, that was all. There could have been one or two pistols in that group that I was with. And that was personal weapons, but I didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say those were civilian uniforms. Did you have any patches, anything to show that you were a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, not at that time. I had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you issued with those, that is, with the uniform and some insignia to be identified by as members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: After that, since I had my car, and there was a shortage of diesel fuel, so I was reattached to the staff which was next to the department store in Sarajevo. It was then that I was issued with a uniform, and we then guarded -- or rather, we guarded the entrance. We took shifts to check who goes into the building, who comes out of the building, something like a janitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you could tell us, this headquarters where you reported, where you were issued with the uniform and placed your vehicle at the disposal of the army, whose headquarters was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the chief headquarters of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the headquarters of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I'm not sure. No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what military formation had this headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I've no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you made the declaration that you would be speaking the truth. Can you tell us what kind of identification card did you have on the basis of which you went -- you reported to that? What did this card say? What formation was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I really can't remember. The cards said the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said that you had placed your car at the disposal of the BH army, what did you do with that vehicle? Did you use it and for what purposes did you use it in the service of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I was meant to use the car, but as of the moment when I was mobilised to that unit, the vehicle never left the compound. I only worked there as a night watch, at the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that was what street and which building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Next to the department store. It was Vranica, across the street from the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And which part of the city of Sarajevo is it where the Vranica enterprise was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Centar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Centar, what street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Titova on one side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And on the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't know what it was called, whether it was the JNA, whether it was the JNA Street or the street of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it in the part of -- was in the locality called Cengic Vila?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you -- how much time did you spend at the positions where the headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I would be on a 12-hour duty, and then I would have I think three days off. Because we were I think eight to ten men, so we took shifts of 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That building, was it a residential or an office building or a commercial building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was a commercial building, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the eight of you who guarded this building, how many other troops were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which commanders came to that headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long -- you said it was until October 1993 when your wife fell victim. Did you go there every day during the time, or depending on your assignment schedule?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, depending on the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence would like to show the witness the map 3668, which is the Prosecution's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness AF, you have in front of the map -- the map where you identified the Sedrenik, the house of your parents, and the place of the position called Spicasta Stijena. Can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I, with your leave, just check something on that map. Could it be removed from the ELMO immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mentioned that you think that the yellow sticker should be a bit further down as well. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, there is an area that I think should be covered as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we please enlarge the area covered by a yellow sticker a bit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you please mark the place where the headquarters of the military formation was. You say you don't know what it was called, where you stood guard. Will you please take the black marker and circle it. And will you put number 1. Witness AF, can you read maps at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, I'm not much of a strategic expert, but I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, being a taxi driver, you must know the streets in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, madam, but it was six or seven years ago and many streets have changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I only want to ask you to circle place where the headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, it is roughly somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please place 1 there and tell us what is that area called, the one that you've circled.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, you can see some buildings between the former Misirbina and Titova Streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Your Honour, the witness has circled as the location of the headquarters of the military formation he belonged to, where he worked, according to the witness on the corner of Marsal Tito Street, and the other street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what was the name of the other street, for the record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Misirbina and Titova.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And he has put number 1 in the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It is only approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you say you would have two or three days off. Do you have any knowledge if in the area of Vratnik or Kovaci localities, that 1993, the 2nd Mountain Brigade of the army of the BH had its positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the positions were in relation to the locality of Vratnik where you lived of the army of BH and the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: They were in the part of the city which is behind the Vratnik, which is called Ophodza.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you draw it on the map. Will you mark the positions of the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If it's possible, please circle that area which is part of the Vratnik neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you could please mark a number 2 right inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness indicated with a number 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it's important for the transcript that we describe whatever a witness did if it leaves no traces on the photograph or on the map. But if you invite the witness to mark a circle with a 2, everyone will later see the circle and the 2. So if you just confirm that the witness marked a circle with a 2, it's not necessary any more to describe the area because everyone can see where it is later on on the map. So it's only if what the witness did leaves no traces that it is necessary to describe precisely what he did for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you please move your microphone a bit upwards and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Place it on the plastic thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's even suggested that you place it on the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The protective measures, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's caused by the protective measures that they have difficulties in hearing you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. AF, could you within that circle indicated with a number 2 tell us where the positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were and where the VRS positions were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: They were inside -- they were not inside the circle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if they were outside the circle, could you tell us if they were, in fact, outside the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Ophodza are not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far are or were the positions of the BH army from the circle that you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: They are in Ophodza, in that neighbourhood, so that's what the difference is. In metres, I couldn't really tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, approximately -- I don't know. I wouldn't really want to give an approximate evaluation. I will show it to you on the map if you have a map that shows Ophodza.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if in the area of Borije and of this place for which you say is called Ophodza were there any fights between those two armies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in regards to this circle, how far is Borije from this circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't want to cause any confusion whatsoever in giving you the wrong measurements. If you do have a map with Borije and Ophodza, I will show it to you on that map. I do not wish to give you too much or too less --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimate in terms of kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Really, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the day when your wife perished, can you tell us if in that part of the city some fightings were going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us at what time this took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: About noon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993, did you ever hear that some fightings were going on in that part of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: We would hear shots, shelling took place from Borije. We could hear it and we could also see it with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that this was easy to see, from which vantage point were you able to see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, approximately let's say -- actually who was brave enough to go behind Vratnik? There is an old tower, and from this tower it was very easy with the naked eye to see Borije.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you're telling us that you were able to see Borije, you also said that Borije was under the control of the VRS, can you then tell us if Ophodza was closer to Vratnik or was it closer to Borije?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Ophodza is located between Borije and Vratnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So therefore you're telling us that the ABiH positions were closer to Vratnik than to Borije where the VRS positions were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that Ophodza was held by the BH army; you're telling us it was closer to Vratnik, that area was closer to Vratnik than to Borije?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Ophodza is closer to Vratnik than it is to Borije.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, therefore, how far were they distanced from one another, those two armies? What was the distance between the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I really wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often did the shelling occur from Borije in the direction of the area of Vratnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: On a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "on a daily basis," are you talking about shells that were fired and also were there any other projectiles being fired? Did you hear any other shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't know how to answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you would hear these projectiles being fired from the Borije areas you said, would you be able to hear some other weapons fire as you said that you could hear firing but were there any other weapons involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, only that. I don't know what weapons are you talking about exactly? Are you talking about rifles and that kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, tell us, you said that you heard that some projectiles were fired. From what kind of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to hear if some shots were also fired from a lighter -- from some lighter weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Coming from that direction, did you ever hear some light weaponry shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember or you never heard such a thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about the time when your wife died, you said that during that period you were a member of the army of BiH. How often would you go to the area where your parents lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: On a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked an area with a cross, it's the area where your parents lived. Do you know if the 105th Motorised Brigade of the BH army was located there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I know that the army was located in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us whether the positions of the 105th Motorised Brigade were in the area of Grdonj and Sedam Suma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this map that position, the positions therefore of Grdonj, Sedam Suma, the seven woods, and Streziste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: You want me to write it down, mark it down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you please tell Ms. Pilipovic to put her microphone on the plastic because we can't hear her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please put your microphone on the plastic -- or if the usher would help Ms. Pilipovic to put the microphone closer to her face. It's all caused by the protective measures. It's not your fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we're facing these difficulties. If you would perhaps for the remaining minutes bend over to the microphone very precise. I know that I'm asking you perhaps too much, and that it will disturb your concentration on what you're doing. But unfortunately the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. AF, can you please indicate on the map the positions of the 105th Motorised Brigade located in the area of Sedam Suma, seven woods, Grdonj, and Streziste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I can tell you where mark down where Grdonj, Streziste is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, these four circles are Grdonj and to the right you have Streziste.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, there is a line drawn above Sedam Suma, and to the right there's a right line, and that indicates the area of Streziste. The line to the left where Sedam Suma is also where Grdonj is. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, it's written here. Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked this down with respect to Spicasta Stijena now. Can you tell us that it is between Spicasta Stijena -- no Grdonj, Streziste and Sedam Suma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in 1993 and 1994 in that area, if fightings took place between the 105th Motorised Brigade and the members of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 1992, 1993, up until the month of August 1994. Could you tell us for that period of time if that was the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often were those fightings going on, what frequency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far were the front lines, one from the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I've never been there. I've never gone to the field at that spot, so I can't really tell you where it is and how far they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that members of your family died during the conflict. Can you tell us if those members who died were also members of the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From the members of the family, from my family who died, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any able-bodied men in your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Only myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in 1992, 1993, 1994, the front lines ever changed in that part of Sedrenik where the 105th Motorised Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence would like to submit to the witness some photographs. P3131 is the document in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Ms. Pilipovic. May I assume that somewhere in the next 10 or 12 minutes, you'd be able to conclude the cross-examination? You said a few minutes extra.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, I will try to do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because you'll understand that it's not because I'm becoming impatient, but I have to take care of those who assist us in the booth as well. And I think all those in the booth are aware that they are on a Friday, and the consequences of not being able to finish this cross-examination. But when I do not hear any loud objections at this very moment, I assume -- I hope at least that we can continue. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at picture number 2. Can you confirm to us if we see here Spicasta Stijena, if that's the general area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were the positions of the VRS and what military formation was here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was all over Spicasta Stijena on it. Now, as regards for the formation, I really couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell us, if you look at picture number 3, in what direction is it towards the north, south, east, or west, that Spicasta Stijena lies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It is to the left side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, that would be in the westerly direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the Sedam Suma, the seven woods, is also there on this hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I just ask that the question be re-asked --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I ask that we get oral answers from the witness in respect to the question that he's asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps Mr. AF, if you nod, it cannot be translated. It will not be in the transcript. So would you please answer the questions. And Ms. Pilipovic, if you ask whether Spicasta Stijena is on the north, west, east, or the south, could you please indicate to the north, the south, or the west or east of what exactly? Because I mean every place in the world is always to the east, to the north, to the south, and to the west of another place.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, would you be able to tell us what is the hill that we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Are you talking about this hill without any trees? It does not represent anything. It used to be a wooded hill. But people needed to cut wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We do see a bare hill here behind Sedam Suma, seven woods.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose that this is where it begins. It begins from there. It's a very large region. The seven woods' area is quite large.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you talk to us about the left part of the wooded area for which you say that seven woods lies, Sedam Suma, you said that your house was there. But is Spicasta Stijena also on that part, on that side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you told us that Sedam Suma was under the control of the ABiH, and as to Spicasta Stijena, that you've identified to us was under the control of the VRS. Can you, therefore, confirm if in that area there were fightings going on between those two armies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I couldn't really confirm this to you because I do not know. I did not live there. Do you understand me? I used to live in Vratnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you, therefore, tell us in terms of kilometres what is the distance between Mrkovici and Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Right behind Spicasta Stijena, we can get to Mrkovici. But in terms of metres or kilometres, I wouldn't be able to give you the right distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us if Sedam Suma where a part of Streziste is was also the site where the 105th Motorised Brigade was, and the VRS army? Is that right under Mrkovici, or can you tell us if the positions of the VRS were right behind the BH army, or that is to say right behind Vranica, Sedam Suma, and Streziste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that you heard some projectiles being fired, can you tell us what did the sound sound like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: What do you mean, simultaneously or how do you want me to explain it to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you compare to us that sound, can you explain to us what the firing sound was like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was like a sound coming from the depth of -- I don't know how to explain to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you heard a blunt sound coming from afar. Would you be able to tell us from which firing positions was this projectile fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you this, but I was able to hear very clearly that it came from behind Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the distance between that point and the point where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: From where I was, up until Spicasta Stijena, there could have been approximately 150 to 200 metres as the crow flies. So from the place where I was up until Spicasta Stijena. Now, what was going on there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you would go to visit your parents, would they tell you that right under Spicasta Stijena the BH army positions were and that those positions were held by the members of the 105th Motorised Brigade; in other words, able-bodied men from Sedrenik, civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that a witness who just testified before you who lives in Sedrenik, she told us that the BH army positions were deployed right under Spicasta Stijena, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No, I would not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the JNA, that you did your military service, in terms of time, how much does it take for a projectile fly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in terms of minutes when is it that you heard the projectile? What was the lapse of time that elapsed between the firing and the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Maybe 10 seconds. Do you understand me? About from 10 to 20 seconds. I can't really tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that a projectile's flight is 24 seconds, how can you then explain that you heard when the projectile was fired and when it exploded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was precisely 15 seconds. I said between 10 to 15, maybe 20 seconds, the time elapsed between the firing and the explosion. I didn't really measure this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us earlier that on 31st March, 1993, your father died from a sniping bullet and your mother was injured. Would you know, could you tell us if on that day where your parents lived there was some fightings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: It was a very quiet day. There was no fightings going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this or did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I know this, and I'm sure of it at a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did somebody confirm this to you or did you just infer this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I know that it was a very quiet day. There was no fighting going on aside from the sniper activity from the Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what a sniper is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Sniper? Well, a sniper is a rifle on which is mounted -- how do you call it, an optical device which can enable you to see the target from afar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You followed the training as a soldier. Did you ever see a sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict that took place in 1992, 1993, and 1994, up until the month of August, with regards to the territory of Sarajevo, did you ever see somebody who was shooting from a sniper gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what, therefore, can you tell us that from Spicasta Stijena there was sniping activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you only hear that? Was it hearsay, because you told me that you never saw anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Well, I think that without a sniper being hidden there, you can't really target anything at that distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you confirming to us that the front line in relation to the house where your parents lived was 100, 150 metres away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: Thereabouts, roughly. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, am I mistaken? I think this is the third or the fourth time that the same question is put to the witness and that is answered similarly. I mean, it's so repetitious on many aspects, the last 30 seconds you asked twice whether he had ever seen a sniper. That is within 30 seconds you asked it twice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has concluded its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I have no...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Nieto-Navia will now put one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Witness -- Mr. Usher, could you please show the witness the map, 3668. You drew a circle with the number 2 to the right part of the map. What exactly were you indicating with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF
utterances.text: I marked the neighbourhood where I lived, Vratnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Chamber has no further questions for you, Mr. AF, I'd like to tell you that this Chamber is aware of how difficult it might have been for you to testify on not just one but several very painful events in your life. On the other hand, I hope that you understand how important it is for this Court to hear from those who have been at these locations and at these times, what their answers are to the questions put by both the Prosecution and the Defence to those persons because your answers to the questions of the parties and the questions of the Judges will assist us in preparing the decisions we'll have to take in this case. We also are aware that apart from being taken back to these painful events, that you do it far from home. You had to travel a long distance to come to The Hague. You certainly will have had to wait for quite some time before you could come into this courtroom. We are aware of how difficult that is, and we would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and assisting everyone in this courtroom in performing our tasks. Thank you very much, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, could you please assist us in dealing with the documents which will not take much time, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. President, if perhaps the witness could be escorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it could be done, yes. This is no problem with the... Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2424 under seal, diagram drawn by witness. Exhibit P3131, a set of photographs under seal. P3668, a map marked by witness under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3667 was already -- so the name sheet 3667 was admitted in evidence already before. Then all these documents have been admitted in evidence. Then finally, I first of all would like to thank especially all those who assist us, not always very good visible behind their smoked glasses. But that you enabled the Chamber to conclude the examination of the witness this week so that he could return home. Thank you very much for that.
