Mr. Stamp, as far as I understand, the order will be that the witness which is still -- which is in The Hague could be examined Monday morning first, and as soon as we concluded the examination of that witness, that we'll then go into the videolink and hear the other witnesses from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As it pleases you, Mr. President, Your Honours. May I also point out to the Court that the witnesses for whom protective measures were granted, there were another couple of witnesses if I may refer to them by the pseudonyms they have been given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding that -- have you seen the decision given by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, a copy was made available to me by the Registrar this morning. The orders were made in respect to Witness AG and Witness AH. They are here. And I would hope that the Court could leave it to our discretion as to whether they could be sent back and brought back, because the decision to some extent depends on advice which we have to receive from the Victim Witnesses Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes as far as I understand but if I'm mistaken please inform me, if there are witness that could be heard within let's say a reasonable period of time, we would then first examine those witnesses so that we are able to send them home afterwards. But I don't know how many witnesses are waiting. I was informed that it was just one. But am I well informed now that there are more?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My information, and perhaps I might need some time to confirm this, is that there would be three left. It had been indicated that of those three, the two I just mentioned, perhaps might need to be sent back, to return, because they might take some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that then I think my information and your information coincides to the point that they will be one remaining after you have sent back two of them. Yes. I think that would be acceptable, and of course we leave it to some extent also to you and to the Victims and Witness Unit how to deal with witnesses present. This Chamber, of course, is very much trying to make sure that witnesses are not unnecessarily sent back before they have been examined. So for the time being, I would say we expect one witness to be examined next Monday morning. We do not expect at this very moment two other witnesses. If you change your mind, would you then please be in touch with the senior legal officer, and at least members of this Chamber are here this afternoon. So for the time being, I would say the one witness you had in mind that would stay during the weekend will be examined next Monday morning, and no others. But if for any practical reasons you think it should be done otherwise, please -- but then inform us as soon as possible. Yes? No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Lastly, Mr. President, Your Honours, in respect to Exhibit P2171, the report which you had ordered be redacted, at least that the translation be redacted. We have here the redacted version as ordered by the Court, and we hope, we trust that it will done in a manner which pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that we don't have to take a decision on that right away. And since Ms. Pilipovic is not reading and speaking English, I would suggest to you that you give a copy already now to Ms. Pilipovic so that she can confer with her colleague and consult him, and that we take a decision then in the beginning of next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As it pleases you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's nothing else, I once again thanks our assistants for enabling us to conclude the examination of the witness today. I wish you all a good weekend, and we'll adjourn until next Monday, 9.30, in this same courtroom. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2.14 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of March, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.
